summaryBox.takeaway: Methanogenic archaebacteria (Methanobacterium) anaerobically digest cellulosic material to generate combustible Biogas (50-70% CH4, 30-40% CO2). Gobar gas plants use cattle dung slurry in concrete digesters with floating gasholders; technology standardized by IARI and KVIC.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 7.1 Methanogens & Natural Habitats
- **Methanogens**: Obligate anaerobic archaebacteria (such as ***Methanobacterium***) that synthesize methane gas by catabolizing cellulosic substrates and volatile organic acids under strictly anaerobic conditions:
  $$\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
  $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_4 + \text{CO}_2$$
- **Natural Habitats**:
  1. Anaerobic sludge in STPs (digesting aerobic bacterial/fungal flocs).
  2. Waterlogged marshy and swampy soils ("Marsh Gas").
  3. **Rumen of Herbivorous Cattle**: Essential for digesting dietary cellulose; consequently, cattle dung (**Gobar**) is rich in methanogens and serves as ideal feedstock.

### 7.2 Biogas Composition Spectrum
- **Methane ($\text{CH}_4$)**: **$50\text{--}70\%$** (Primary combustible fuel gas).
- **Carbon Dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$)**: $30\text{--}40\%$.
- **Hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) & Hydrogen Sulfide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$)**: Trace concentrations ($1\text{--}5\%$).
- **Oxygen ($\text{O}_2$)**: Strictly **ABSENT** ($0\%$) because methanogenesis is an obligate anaerobic process.

### 7.3 Rural Biogas Plant Components & Indian Leadership
1. **Concrete Digester Tank**: $10\text{--}15\text{ feet}$ deep pit where dung-and-water slurry ($1:1$ ratio) is collected.
2. **Floating Cover / Gasholder**: Steel or fiberglass dome placed over slurry that rises as methane gas accumulates.
3. **Gas Outlet**: Pipeline connected to the gas dome that supplies fuel for cooking and lighting in village homes.
4. **Spent Sludge Outlet**: Digested slurry is extracted through an overflow chamber and dried for use as rich **organic manure / fertilizer**.
- **Indian R&D Pioneers**: Biogas technology in India was developed and deployed via collaborative initiatives between the **Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI)** and the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Three Stages of Anaerobic Digestion
conceptBreakdown.title: Three Stages of Anaerobic Digestion
conceptBreakdown.content: Anaerobic digestion proceeds via: (1) Hydrolysis (complex polymers broken into monomers by extracellular enzymes); (2) Acidogenesis / Acetogenesis (monomers converted to volatile fatty acids and acetic acid); (3) Methanogenesis (methanogens convert acetate and H2/CO2 into CH4).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Calorific Value of Biogas
conceptBreakdown.title: Calorific Value of Biogas
conceptBreakdown.content: Biogas has a high calorific value of 20–25 MJ/m³ and burns cleanly with a non-luminous blue flame without producing smoke or soot, making it an eco-friendly rural energy alternative to firewood.
